# FPGA project (1.4) — FIR active noise cancellation

This directory contains the SystemVerilog skeleton for the on-board version
of the filter described in `notebooks/1_2_fir_filter_16bit.ipynb`. The
pipeline is:

```
INMP441 mic --I2S--> mic_driver --> fir_filter --> inverter --> spk_driver --I2S--> PCM5102 DAC
```

* Coefficients are Q1.15 `int16`, generated by the Streamlit app
  (`app/streamlit_app.py`) and pasted into [`rtl/coeffs.sv`](rtl/coeffs.sv).
* The math is bit-identical to `filter_anc.filter_fixed.apply_filter_fixed_q15`,
  so the Python model serves as a golden reference for the testbench.

## Reference / drivers

The plan is to reuse the I2S microphone driver (INMP441) and I2S audio output
driver (PCM5102) from the educational repository
[**`basics-graphics-music`**](https://github.com/yuri-panchul/basics-graphics-music).
That repository already contains board support packages, the I2S drivers and
example top-level wrappers. Drop the modules in this folder into the project
tree of `basics-graphics-music` (or vendor the drivers here when the target
board is selected).

## Files

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| [`rtl/fir_filter.sv`](rtl/fir_filter.sv) | Parameterized Q1.15 direct-form FIR |
| [`rtl/inverter.sv`](rtl/inverter.sv) | Sample inverter (×−1) with saturation |
| [`rtl/coeffs.sv`](rtl/coeffs.sv) | `B_TAPS` localparam generated from the Streamlit UI |
| [`rtl/top.sv`](rtl/top.sv) | Top-level wiring mic_driver → fir → inverter → spk_driver |
| [`tb/tb_fir_filter.sv`](tb/tb_fir_filter.sv) | Self-checking testbench against a Python reference vector |

## Target board

Not yet fixed. `basics-graphics-music` supports a wide range of platforms
(Sipeed Tang Nano 9K, iCEBreaker, Intel/Altera DE10-Lite, Xilinx Arty/Basys 3,
etc.). The chosen target only affects:

* Pin / I/O constraints (BSP file in `basics-graphics-music`).
* The build toolchain (Vivado / Quartus / Gowin / yosys+nextpnr).

The RTL itself is platform-agnostic.

## Verifying against the Python model

```
python -m pytest tests/                           # software equivalence
# Then, with your FPGA toolchain of choice, run tb_fir_filter.sv against
# golden vectors produced from filter_anc.apply_filter_fixed_q15.
```
